name: iJustine
milestone_by_age_26: Launched the iJustine YouTube channel with first videos on May 12, 2006 at age 22, then broke out in 2007 (age 23) with a viral video documenting a 300-page iPhone bill that brought millions of views and mainstream tech-creator fame.
early_history_summary: Justine Ezarik, born March 20, 1984 in Pittsburgh, graduated Pittsburgh Technical Institute (2004) and became one of the earliest full-time tech/lifestyle YouTubers. Combined gadget reviews, vlogs, and Apple-centric content as the platform scaled from 2006 onward.
family_context_summary: Born Pittsburgh, PA; father Steve Ezarik (coal miner per some profiles), mother Michelle a physical education teacher; has sisters who also created content.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not tech-media professionals; sister collaborators later amplified channel work.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early YouTube, viral iPhone bill, Apple tech culture, multi-channel creator
evidence_summary: iJustine's ≤26 milestones are channel launch (2006, 22) and viral 300-page iPhone bill (2007, 23)—classic early-YouTube distribution breakout. Platform timing and consistent tech/lifestyle production dominate; family wealth/domain pipelines are weak.
starting_point: Born 1984 in Pittsburgh to a working-class family; tech-school graduate who entered early YouTube tech content.
current_position: Long-running tech/lifestyle YouTuber with multi-million subscribers; still active on YouTube and related creator platforms.

trajectory.event: Posted first iJustine YouTube videos, entering the early creator economy.
Viral 300-page iPhone bill video brought mainstream attention.
Established as a top tech YouTuber with expanding brand deals and multi-channel presence.
Continued as a leading female tech creator with mainstream media crossovers.

name: Unbox Therapy
milestone_by_age_26: Lewis Hilsenteger co-created the Unbox Therapy YouTube channel in December 2010 at about age 25, founding one of the definitive tech unboxing brands (later tens of millions of subscribers).
early_history_summary: Canadian creator who started Unbox Therapy while working in a small computer repair shop, pairing plainspoken product unboxings with high-volume gadget reviews as YouTube tech media professionalized.
family_context_summary: Born Toronto area, Canada; detailed parental occupations not central in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: YouTube unboxing wave, PC repair domain, Jack McCann collaboration, Bendgate virality later
evidence_summary: Unbox Therapy channel founding December 2010 at age ~25 is the ≤26 milestone for this brand row (same human as Lewis Hilsenteger). YouTube platform timing and consumer-electronics domain immersion are primary advantages.
starting_point: Born 1985 in Toronto area; computer-repair background before founding Unbox Therapy on YouTube.
current_position: Host/founder of Unbox Therapy, a top global tech unboxing channel (tens of millions of subscribers); also Lew Later and related brands.

trajectory.event: Co-created Unbox Therapy YouTube channel with Jack McCann.
iPhone 6 Plus 'Bendgate' video went massively viral, accelerating mainstream fame.
Unbox Therapy ranked among the largest tech review channels worldwide.

name: Lewis Hilsenteger
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Unbox Therapy with Jack McCann in December 2010 at age 25, building a defining consumer-tech unboxing and review channel from a Toronto-area base.
early_history_summary: Lewis George Hilsenteger (born May 6, 1985, Toronto) studied at Toronto School of Art, worked in computer repair, and turned gadget unboxing into a full-time media business that later included the viral iPhone Bendgate moment.
family_context_summary: Born Toronto, Ontario; lives Greater Toronto Area; family financial details not well documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: YouTube, unboxing format, PC repair shop domain, Bendgate
evidence_summary: Same core milestone as Unbox Therapy brand row: December 2010 channel founding at age 25. Platform-native YouTube growth plus hands-on electronics domain exposure drive the leverage story.
starting_point: Born 1985 in Toronto; art school and computer-repair path into tech YouTube.
current_position: Canadian tech YouTuber best known as Unbox Therapy host; multi-channel creator with massive global audience.

trajectory.event: Launched Unbox Therapy YouTube channel.
Bendgate iPhone video became a global news moment.
Sustained Unbox Therapy as a top-tier tech review franchise.

name: Felix Kjellberg
milestone_by_age_26: Registered the PewDiePie YouTube channel on April 29, 2010 at age 20 and rapidly became the defining Let's Play / comedy-gaming creator of the early 2010s, reaching industry-leading subscriber counts well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Felix Arvid Ulf Kjellberg, born October 24, 1989 in Gothenburg, Sweden; dropped industrial economics studies to pursue YouTube full-time. Built horror-game commentary style and 'Bro Army' community into the most-subscribed channel for years.
family_context_summary: Raised Gothenburg; mother Johanna former CIO at clothing firm KappAhl; father Ulf a company CEO per fan/wiki sources—middle/upper professional household.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were business executives, not entertainment creators; provided relative economic safety rather than media pipeline.
primary_early_advantage_tags: YouTube gaming wave, Let's Play format, Bro Army community, full-time creator bet
evidence_summary: PewDiePie channel creation at 20 (2010) and hypergrowth through mid-20s are clear ≤26 milestones. YouTube platform wave, intense production, and gaming-domain fluency dominate; family offered modest financial safety, not entertainment networks.
starting_point: Born 1989 in Gothenburg, Sweden to professional parents; left university to pursue YouTube gaming content full-time.
current_position: Swedish YouTuber PewDiePie; long among the platform's most influential creators; married to Marzia Kjellberg; continues content with reduced peak mainstream controversy profile.

trajectory.event: Created PewDiePie YouTube channel after losing access to earlier PewDie account.
Became YouTube's most-subscribed channel, defining Let's Play comedy.
Reached unprecedented subscriber scale and global cultural recognition.
Lost most-subscribed title to T-Series after multi-year public race; remained top individual creator.

name: Tyler Blevins
milestone_by_age_26: Began playing Halo 3 professionally in 2009 at about age 18 (MLG circuit), establishing a multi-year esports career with teams including Cloud9 and Team Liquid well before the Fortnite streaming explosion.
early_history_summary: Richard Tyler Blevins, born June 5, 1991 in Taylor, Michigan; raised Lake Villa, Illinois. Competed in Halo esports from 2009, later streamed full-time, and became the face of Fortnite streaming after 2017–18 with record-breaking concurrent viewers.
family_context_summary: Midwest US upbringing; worked fast food while grinding early esports; detailed parental occupations not central in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as an esports family pipeline.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Halo pro circuit, long streaming reps, Fortnite cultural wave, Twitch distribution
evidence_summary: Pro Halo start in 2009 at ~18 qualifies as ≤26 material milestone; Fortnite Drake stream (Mar 2018, still age 26) is a later peak. Years of competitive reps plus platform distribution explain leverage; family capital not documented.
starting_point: Born 1991 Michigan; Illinois-raised competitive gamer who entered pro Halo while still a teen.
current_position: Major Twitch/YouTube streamer (Ninja); diversified into lifestyle content and brands; remains one of the best-known Western streamers.

trajectory.event: Entered professional Halo 3 competition on the MLG circuit.
Began streaming competitive gaming content more regularly.
Fortnite stream with Drake set Twitch concurrent-viewer records; became global celebrity streamer.
High-profile exclusive deal moves between Mixer and Twitch; peak commercial era.

name: Bugha
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Fortnite World Cup 2019 Solo Finals on July 28, 2019 at age 16, earning $3 million and becoming the first solo Fortnite world champion.
early_history_summary: Kyle Giersdorf, born December 30, 2002, Pottsgrove/Pennsylvania area. Rose through competitive Fortnite to Sentinels and the inaugural World Cup, then sustained FNCS-level play and streaming career as a teen champion.
family_context_summary: Pennsylvania suburban teen; family supported competitive gaming path around World Cup era; detailed wealth/occupation data limited in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not a traditional sports-academy pipeline; family logistics support around events is noted anecdotally.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Fortnite World Cup, teen mechanical skill, battle-royale esports wave, Sentinels
evidence_summary: World Cup Solo win at 16 is an unambiguous ≤26 tier-defining milestone with multi-source documentation. Peak competitive skill plus Fortnite cultural wave are the core drivers.
starting_point: Born 2002 in Pennsylvania; teenage competitive Fortnite player who won the inaugural World Cup.
current_position: Professional Fortnite player/streamer (Bugha); multi-time FNCS contender and one of the most recognized Fortnite competitors globally.

trajectory.event: Won Fortnite World Cup Solo Finals for $3M prize.
Won FNCS championship titles, sustaining elite competitive status.
Additional FNCS championship success; long-term org and streaming presence.

name: N0tail
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Fnatic's European Dota 2 roster on March 30, 2012 at age 18 after HoN success, becoming a top-tier professional player; later co-founded OG and won The International twice (2018–19), still within/near the age-26 window for TI8.
early_history_summary: Johan Sundstein, born October 8, 1993, Danish/Faroese. Pro from mid-teens in Heroes of Newerth, transitioned to Dota 2 with Fnatic (2012), then co-founded OG and became the first two-time TI champion.
family_context_summary: Danish/Faroese background; detailed parental occupations not richly documented in English sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as an esports family pipeline.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Fnatic, OG founding, TI back-to-back, HoN-to-Dota transition
evidence_summary: Fnatic join at 18 (2012) is a clear ≤26 pro milestone; TI8 win (2018, age 24) and TI9 (2019, age 25) are historic. Complementary elite teammates and long competitive reps are primary advantages.
starting_point: Born 1993 in Denmark (Faroese roots); teenage HoN/Dota professional who joined Fnatic at 18.
current_position: Dota 2 legend; OG founder/player-turned-coach; among highest career prize earners in esports history.

trajectory.event: Joined Fnatic EU Dota 2 roster after HoN career.
Co-founded OG esports organization with teammates.
Won The International 2018 with OG.
Won The International 2019—first back-to-back TI champion player/org era.
Transitioned toward coaching/leadership roles after long playing career.

name: Jared Isaacman
category: Payments founder / commercial astronaut / NASA administrator
milestone_by_age_26: Founded United Bank Card (later Harbortouch / Shift4 Payments) in 1999 at age 16 after leaving high school, building a point-of-sale payments company he has led as CEO since inception.
early_history_summary: Born February 11, 1983 Summit, NJ; youngest of four; left Ridge High School at 16 for full-time entrepreneurship (later GED and Embry-Riddle online BS). Scaled payments firm while becoming an elite pilot and later private astronaut.
family_context_summary: Born to Donald and Sandra Marie Isaacman; Jewish family in New Jersey suburbs (Union Township, Westfield, Liberty Corner); not portrayed as inherited payments dynasty.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents not documented as payments-industry operators; early independence and school-leaving are emphasized over family business transfer.
primary_early_advantage_tags: teen founder, Shift4 payments, pilot/astronaut path, execution intensity
evidence_summary: United Bank Card founding at 16 (1999) is a strong ≤26 founder milestone with multi-source confirmation. Execution intensity and long operating tenure dominate; later spaceflight and NASA role are post-26 achievements built on that base.
starting_point: Born 1983 in Summit, New Jersey; left high school at 16 to found a payments company full-time.
current_position: 15th NASA Administrator (sworn in Dec 2025); Shift4 founder; Inspiration4 and Polaris Dawn commercial astronaut; billionaire entrepreneur-pilot.

trajectory.event: Founded United Bank Card (later Shift4 Payments) as a teen entrepreneur.
Set world record circumnavigating the globe in a light jet (~62 hours).
Co-founded Draken International fighter-jet adversary training company.
Took Shift4 public; recognized as billionaire.
Commanded Inspiration4, first all-civilian orbital mission.
Led Polaris Dawn; first private citizen spacewalk (SEVA).
Confirmed and sworn in as NASA Administrator.

name: Chris Messina
milestone_by_age_26: Proposed the Twitter hashtag in a public tweet on August 23, 2007 at age 26 (#barcamp), creating the social-media convention later adopted globally for topic grouping.
early_history_summary: Christopher Reaves Messina, born January 7, 1981 in Bedford, New Hampshire; Carnegie Mellon communication design graduate (2003). Open-source advocate and product designer who pushed hashtags as a lightweight, non-patented social protocol.
family_context_summary: Born Bedford, NH; detailed parental occupations not central in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as a tech family pipeline.
primary_early_advantage_tags: CMU design, early Twitter SF scene, open-source advocacy, hashtag protocol
evidence_summary: Hashtag proposal August 23, 2007 at age 26 is a clearly dated, multi-source material milestone. Early SF social-web immersion, CMU design training, and platform wave timing are the main advantages; he notably did not patent the idea.
starting_point: Born 1981 in Bedford, New Hampshire; Carnegie Mellon design graduate who entered early Silicon Valley social-web scenes.
current_position: Product designer, speaker, and open-source advocate known as inventor of the hashtag; consulting and public speaking on product/social design.

trajectory.event: Graduated Carnegie Mellon in communication design.
Tweeted the original hashtag proposal for Twitter groups (#barcamp).
Hashtags became mainstream on Twitter during major news events.
Widely celebrated 10-year anniversary of the hashtag as a global communication standard.

evidence_summary: Influential early weblogger and later Yahoo product designer, but defining institutional milestones cluster after mid-20s; eligibility not forced given birth-year ambiguity and weak two-source ≤26 founder bar.

name: Tantek Çelik
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Microsoft in March 1997 at about age 22 and became a principal engineer on Internet Explorer/CSS (including Mac IE / Tasman-related web standards work), establishing a career-defining systems role in browser CSS implementation well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Turkish-American computer scientist who worked at Microsoft (1997–2004) on CSS and browser technology, later Technorati chief technologist, microformats co-founder/editor, and Mozilla web standards lead.
family_context_summary: Turkish-American background; detailed early family finances not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Microsoft IE/CSS, web standards, later microformats, Mozilla
evidence_summary: Microsoft hire and IE/CSS engineering from 1997 (age ~22) is the ≤26 milestone; microformats leadership is later (mid-2000s). Scarce browser-standards skill and Microsoft ecosystem access dominate advantages.
starting_point: Born ~1975; Turkish-American engineer who entered Microsoft browser/CSS work in his early 20s.
current_position: Web standards lead / open-web technologist long associated with Mozilla and microformats; continues independent web standards advocacy.

trajectory.event: Joined Microsoft; advanced CSS/IE web standards engineering.
Left Microsoft; later became Technorati chief technologist.
Helped launch and edit microformats as open data formats for the web.
Joined Mozilla as web standards lead shaping Firefox platform expectations.
